content:
maya (support): Customer ACME-42 reports invoice shows ~18k tokens billed for last 24h but their API dashboard reports ~12k served. They're upset. asking for a quick triage.

sam (support): Can you paste the invoice id and an example request id? Also did they use any Dedicated/Private deployment or hosted?

maya (support): Invoice INV-2025-03-12-909, customer says most traffic was hosted. Example request_id: req_0a7f3c. They said a large fraction of requests are short prompts (~30 tokens).

owen (billing): I pulled the invoice. Metered_tokens=18522, billed_amount matches. I also checked aggregate logs and found a cluster of requests around 1759234000-1759237000 where metered_tokens spikes.

chris (eng-runtime): Can you share the API request payload + headers for req_0a7f3c? Also we have a debug endpoint to show per-request accounting: GET /v1/debug/requests/:id/usage (internal). If you can't share, we can pull from logs.

maya (support): Pasting a sanitized request from customer: 

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-v1-large",
  "input": "Summarize the meeting notes:\n- action items\n- owners\n",
  "stream": false,
  "client_request_id": "req_0a7f3c",
  "metadata": {"project": "acme-reports"}
}
```

chris (eng-runtime): Thanks. I ran the debug for req_0a7f3c: 
```
debug usage for req_0a7f3c:
  metered_tokens: 45
  served_tokens: 28
  batch_id: batch_3f1
  batch_size: 22
  kv_cache_hit: true
  kv_cache_prefix_reused: true
```

leila (eng-ml): This is typical when continuous batching and prefix/KV cache interact. Short requests can be coalesced into big batches. Metering is counted at enqueue/batch level in some places vs per-request served tokens after cache deduplication. Two main causes: 1) batching duplication of shared prefixes across requests (we count prefix tokens per queued request when building the batch) and 2) metering hooks run before the KV cache lookup for some historical paths.

maya (support): So meter > served because the meter counted full prompt tokens for each request in the batch, even if KV cache later avoided recomputation?

leila (eng-ml): Exactly. Example: imagine 20 requests sharing a 30-token prefix. We build a batch where the prefix is included once in the fused tensor for runtime, but our legacy metering hook (pre-batching) recorded 30 tokens * 20 requests = 600 metered tokens. After the runtime and KV cache dedupe, model only computed prefix once, so served tokens might be ~30 + small deltas. The net effect: billed (metered) >> served in dashboard.

owen (billing): Historically we billed on the metering events emitted at enqueue time to keep accounting simple and cheap. That was called out in docs but customers miss it. We can consider adjusting how we present 'dashboard served tokens' to call out that it’s post-cache.

sam (support): Customer wants a clear explanation and ideally a credit if the gap is large. Any guidance on thresholds or how to compute "expected billed" vs "naive served"?

chris (eng-runtime): Quick triage steps:
1) Pull the batch_id window and list requests in that batch: ```select request_id, prompt_tokens, was_kv_hit from batches where batch_id='batch_3f1'```
2) Check per-request metering events in the metering stream: ```grep batch_3f1 metering.log | jq .tokens```
3) Compare with runtime served accounting: ```curl -s -H 'X-Req: req_0a7f3c' https://runtime.internal/v1/debug/requests/req_0a7f3c/usage```

I already ran step 1-3 for the spike window: we see 22 requests, each had metered prompt_tokens=30, so metered sum=660; runtime served total for the fused batch reported ~64.

leila (eng-ml): For customer-facing explanation: "Metering counts tokens at enqueue time (before batching and KV cache dedup). Dashboard 'served tokens' is the runtime-level post-cache accounting. Differences are expected when many short, similar requests are batched or served from KV cache." Add note: "This is not double-billing; it's a difference in measurement points. Billing uses the metering stream."

maya (support): Can we provide a one-off reconciliation and optionally a credit?

owen (billing): Policy: for >20% unexplained gap we do manual review. This one looks like legitimate by-design difference. But for goodwill, offer a one-time 10% credit if they were unaware and volume spike was unexpected. I'll draft wording.

sam (support): Also offer them a config change: set `continuous_batching.window_ms` lower or `metering.capture_point=post_kv` (experimental) to make metered tokens closer to served. Do we actually have that flag?

chris (eng-runtime): There's an internal toggle `metering.capture_point` we can flip to emit post-cache events for a given customer id (not GA). We can enable for a short window to show them the delta. Steps: run a flag rollout for customer account 12345, enable debug metering for 1 hour, collect events, then revert. I can do this with on-call approval.

leila (eng-ml): Also recommend they add a small prefix sharding knob on the client if their app issues many near-duplicate prompts. That reduces per-request prefix overhead before batching.

maya (support): OK will communicate: explanation + offer 10% goodwill credit + optional debug window and config recommendations. Owen, can you prepare the credit approval? Chris, please stand by for the debug toggle.

owen (billing): Preparing approval now. ping me in 10. :+1:

devbot (billing-bot): Invoice INV-2025-03-12-909 status: pending_credit_review by owen.

maya (support): Thanks team — I'll send a concise summary to the customer and include the debug offer. Closing internal thread after credit decision. :raised_hands:
